author: raymond91125
body:
Dear all, 

The proposal has been made to obsolete (they are MFs)

Each BP term below is followed by the existing MF term it corresponds to (`--> MF`). Every one of the 43 terms has an exact 1:1 MF counterpart already in GO -- no new MF terms are needed.

Two things to note when reviewing:
- The mitochondrial terms map to the **same** MF as their cytosolic counterparts. There are no separate mitochondrial ligase MFs, because compartment is not a molecular-function distinction. A gene charging tRNA in both compartments takes one MF annotation, not two.
- GO:0070681 is the exception to the 1:1 pattern: the indirect transamidation route corresponds to GO:0050567 glutaminyl-tRNA synthase (glutamine-hydrolyzing) activity, not to a glutamine-tRNA ligase.

author: raymond91125
body:
[Written by Claude]

Worked through all 251 rows of the review spreadsheet. Recommendations, reasoning and quotes from each reference are now in column A. Summary here, because a handful of annotations should **not** follow the general BP --> MF mapping added to the description above.

## The bulk of it is already done

| | rows |
|---|---|
| MF already annotated **from the same reference** | 204 |
| MF already has experimental support, but from a different reference | 21 |
| Needed individual assessment against the paper | 23 |
| Row is already an MF annotation | 3 |

For 204 of 251 rows the curator has already made the corresponding MF annotation from the identical paper, so the BP annotation states nothing the MF does not. Those need no migration at all -- they can be deleted when the terms are obsoleted.

I read the 12 papers behind the remaining 23 rows. Most support a clean move to the paired ligase MF. The exceptions below do not.

## Annotations that should not move to a ligase MF

**ZFIN -- `gtpbp3` (ZFIN:ZDB-GENE-050522-335), PMID:30916346, 6 rows.** Annotated IMP to six mitochondrial aminoacylation terms. gtpbp3 is not a synthetase: *"GTPBP3 is a highly conserved tRNA modifying enzyme for the biosynthesis of tm5U at the wobble position of mitochondrial tRNAGlu, tRNAGln, tRNALys, tRNATrp and tRNALeu(UUR)."* The aminoacylation effect is indirect, and runs the opposite way to what an IMP would imply: *"gtpbp3 knock-out zebrafish displayed the global increases in the aminoacylated efficiencies of mitochondrial tRNAs."* Recommend removing all six. The MF this paper supports is GO:0160236 tRNA 5-taurinomethyluridine synthase activity.

**GeneDB -- `Tb11.01.7110` (UniProtKB:Q381N8), PMID:11792845.** Annotated TAS to methionyl-tRNA aminoacylation, but the paper identifies a formyltransferase, not a synthetase: *"RNA interference assays identify the gene encoding the trypanosomal formylase activity. Whereas the predicted protein is homologous to prokaryotic and mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA(Met) formyltransferases, it has about twice the mass of any of these proteins."* Correct term is GO:0004479 methionyl-tRNA formyltransferase activity.

**UniProt -- `DARS2` (UniProtKB:Q6PI48), PMID:23275545.** Annotated to GO:0070145 mitochondrial **asparaginyl**-tRNA aminoacylation. Q6PI48 is the mitochondrial **aspartyl**-tRNA synthetase, and the paper is titled *"Thermodynamic properties distinguish human mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase from bacterial homolog with same 3D architecture."* There is no asparaginyl content. If kept, the MF is GO:0004815, not GO:0004816 -- though note this is a structure/ITC study of binding rather than catalysis, so GO:0000049 tRNA binding may fit the evidence better.

**ComplexPortal -- ARC1 / MES1 / GUS1, PMID:11069915, 6 rows.** All three complex members were given both glutamyl and methionyl aminoacylation. Arc1p catalyses neither: *"In yeast, two enzymes, the methionyl- and glutamyl-tRNA synthetases associate in vivo with the tRNA-binding protein Arc1p."* Arc1p's supported MF here is GO:0000049 tRNA binding. MES1 has methionyl only (GO:0004825), GUS1 glutamyl only (GO:0004818); the crossed pairs should go.

## Two that need a second opinion

**FlyBase -- `Slimp` (FB:FBgn0051133), PMID:30943413.** The abstract establishes SLIMP as a SerRS2 paralog forming a heterodimer with SerRS2, but never states that SLIMP itself charges tRNA-Ser. An IDA to GO:0004828 is not supported by the abstract alone -- full text, or someone who knows whether SLIMP is catalytically active, would settle it.

**MTBBASE -- `lysX` (UniProtKB:P9WFU7), PMID:19649276.** LysX genuinely carries a fused LysRS domain, but this paper assays lipid composition and mutant phenotypes, not aminoacylation, and the Lys-tRNA produced is used to lysinylate phosphatidylglycerol rather than for translation. Moving to GO:0004824 is defensible on domain grounds; dropping the reference is also reasonable.

## One useful observation for the migration

`Tb-TyrRS` (UniProtKB:Q57WH7, PMID:29581012) appears twice, once under the cytosolic term and once under the mitochondrial one, from a single finding: *"we demonstrate that Tb-TyrRS aminoacylates cytosolic as well as mitochondrial tRNATyr indicating that it is dually localized."* Both rows collapse onto one MF, GO:0004831. Worth watching for during migration so dually-localised enzymes do not end up with two MF annotations where one is correct.

Ontology-side context is on geneontology/go-ontology#15375.

Assignees set from [group-contacts.csv](https://github.com/geneontology/go-site/blob/master/metadata/group-contacts.csv), one per impacted organization, using the "Contact for Annotation Review" column where it is filled in and a Curation-role contact otherwise.

GitHub caps an issue at 10 assignees, and there are 16 impacted groups. Assignments went to the ten largest by annotation count; the remaining groups are @-mentioned below so nobody is silently dropped.

Two notes on the mapping itself, in case the CSV wants tidying:

Reminder of what needs attention, from the [review comment above](https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/6525#issuecomment-5432735049): 204 of 251 rows already carry the paired MF from the same reference and need no work. The rows that do need a decision are concentrated in @ZFIN (gtpbp3, 6 rows), @ComplexPortal (Arc1p/MES1/GUS1, 6 rows), GeneDB, UniProt, FlyBase and MTBBASE.

Correcting my previous assignee comment: it covered only the annotation groups and left the mappings section unowned. Mapping contacts are now assigned. Because GitHub caps assignees at 10, I have re-cut the list so that **assignment tracks how much work a group actually has**, rather than how many rows it appears in. Everyone else is @-mentioned and still on the hook.

## Un-assigned to make room - apologies for the churn, you are still needed

Since GO:0070681 is proposed for obsoletion this mapping needs retiring or retargeting, and there is no contact to route it to. @amandamackie - as EcoCyc, are you the right person for MetaCyc mappings, or is there someone else?
- **@esperetta** is listed as a UniRule mappings contact but is not assignable on this repo, so I used @PedroRaposo, the other UniRule contact.

author: RLovering
body:
Hi Raymond

I realise that you have undertaken an incredible amount of work and this is very impressive.

I am obviously just trying to follow the new GO guidelines but I disagree with your suggestion for the revisions you made for the BHF-UCL annotations. For example for: Q5JTZ9: you suggest: MOVE TO MF - ALREADY DONE. AARS2 already carries GO:0004813 (alanine-tRNA ligase activity) annotated from this same reference (PMID:21549344). The BP annotation adds nothing the MF does not already state, so it can be deleted on obsoletion with no migration and no loss of information.

Currently GO:0070127 (tRNA aminoacylation for mitochondrial protein translation) has the BP parents: GO:0032543 mitochondrial translation, GO:0000959 mitochondrial RNA metabolic process, GO:0006418 tRNA aminoacylation for protein translation (I assume this term will be obsoleted too?) which has the parents GO:0043039   
tRNA charging As well as the CC parent GO:0005739 mitochondrion.

Consequently, AARS2 will no longer be associated with any of these upstream terms which will impact future functional analyses. 

One of the strengths of GO is that the workload of curators is reduced by using the ontology to provide relevant more general parent grouping terms so that the curator does not have to go looking for every single possible relevant GO term. It is challenging enough to get consistent annotations between curators (or even by the same curator) without removing these helpful child terms.

I have added 3 of the parent GO terms to GO:0070127 (tRNA aminoacylation for mitochondrial protein translation) to each of the protein records that you suggested I should edit. I hope that other curators will consider what BP annotations to use to replace the BP terms being changed to MF terms (or just deleted).

Obviously I am retired and I have not been keeping up to date with all the GO revisions, so perhaps there will be no BP terms in the future. 

Also please note that tRNAs are associated with various human diseases https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33658722/

Kind regards

Ruth
